findings.summary: Code is shown before its one-line idea, and the idea bullet holds two points.

findings.summary: The outline point that validating @PathVariable/@RequestParam needs class-level @Validated plus constraints on the params is only a table row, with no explanation or example before page 6.
findings.evidence: "Param, class @Validated | ConstraintViolationException | 500 unless handled" and "Param, Spring 6.1+ | HandlerMethodValidationException | 400"
findings.fix: Add a short block on page 3 with an example such as `@Validated class C { get(@RequestParam @Min(1) int n) }`. State that the class needs @Validated and the constraint sits on the param. Explain that this throws ConstraintViolationException, which differs from MethodArgumentNotValidException. Add one line on why Spring 6.1+ can give HandlerMethodValidationException instead.

findings.summary: A bullet holds two ideas, and its wording is garbled.

findings.summary: The 'Param, class @Validated' row looks like it contradicts the page's "400 for validation failures" framing, with no note placed where a reader would see it.
